deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). I is a finite set with Card I = n+1, i0 ∈ I is a chosen index, and I0 = I∖{i0}. C(I) is the set of isomorphism classes of I-indexed systems of pseudo-lines (X, Σ=(Δ_i)_{i∈I}) in a topological projective plane X. Any two pseudo-lines meet exactly once, transversally. Taking Δ = Δ_{i0} as the 'line at infinity' gives the identification C(I) ≃ C_aff(I0), the affine (Euclidean) arrangements indexed by I0. The subscript 'st' (stable) denotes arrangements stable under small deformation, i.e. simple arrangements with no three pseudo-lines concurrent. This class is S_I-invariant, so all the quotient diagrams of page 1 restrict to it.

This page.
(1) Fix ξ = cl(X, Σ) ∈ C_st(I) ≃ C_aff,st(I0). Each Δ_i (i ∈ I0) meets Δ in exactly one point. By simplicity these n points are distinct. Their cyclic order along the circle Δ gives I0 a 'polygonal structure' I0(ξ) depending on ξ. This is meaningful only when Card I0 ≥ 3. In affine terms it is the cyclic order of the 'slopes'.
(2) Cut X along Δ to get Déc(X, Δ). This is a closed disk D = X̃ whose boundary ∂D is the connected 2-sheeted cover of Δ. Each Δ_i, i ∈ I0, becomes a chord of D joining two antipodal boundary points. The result is a system Σ̃ of chords indexed by I0, pairwise crossing exactly once, with no triple points. This is the classical disk model of RP².
(3) The 2n chord endpoints on ∂D form a 2n-gon Ĩ0(ξ). It carries the antipodal involution and is a 2-sheeted cover of the n-gon I0(ξ).
(4) Now fix once and for all an abstract polygonal set S of order 2n, with antipodism a_S, and put I0 = S/a_S. Grothendieck considers C̃_st(S): stable chord systems whose endpoint set is identified with S ('S-pinned'), modulo S-isomorphism. Recording the I0-indexed affine arrangement gives a natural map C̃_st(S) → C_aff,st(I0).
(5) Next page: the image is C_aff,st(I0, π0), those ξ whose induced polygonal structure is the quotient structure π0 coming from S. The fibre over ξ is the set of polygonal isomorphisms S ≅ Ĩ0(ξ) over I0. It has two elements, exchanged by the antipodism.

Purpose. The aim is to reduce the classification of simple projective pseudo-line arrangements (C(n+1), and affine versions) to a combinatorial object with a fixed boundary: stable chord systems in a disk with a fixed 2n-gon of endpoints. The finite counts on the previous page fit this programme. For n+1 = 6 there are 4 simple arrangements; the fibres of the 'forget the marked line' map have cardinalities 1, 1, 2, 2, summing to the 6 simple affine arrangements of 5 lines. For 5 lines there is a unique simple projective arrangement.
errors: No mathematical error. Small gaps: (i) the polygonal structure needs Card I0 ≥ 3; Grothendieck notes this. (ii) The fibre cardinality 2 holds because C̃_st(S) is taken modulo S-isomorphisms, so automorphisms of ξ do not shrink the fibre. (iii) An arrangement whose cyclic order is π0 composed with a non-dihedral permutation of I0 is not in the image; this is precisely why the image is the subset C_aff,st(I0, π0), as stated on the next page.

'Polygonal structure' presumably means a cyclic order up to reversal (dihedral). The text does not say whether orientation is kept. If the dihedral reading is right, the order-2 group in step (5) comes from the antipode alone, consistent with the claim.

ideas.what: Cutting the projective plane along one pseudo-line gives a disk. The other pseudo-lines become chords with antipodal endpoints on the boundary, which double-covers the cut line.
ideas.modern_name: Disk (hemisphere) model of RP²; Euclidean / marked arrangements; pseudoline arrangement with a line at infinity

ideas.what: Polygonal (cyclic) structure on the index set I0, given by the order of intersection with the line at infinity. The endpoint 2n-gon is its antipodal double cover.
ideas.modern_name: Order at infinity / slope order; local sequences and allowable sequences

ideas.what: Stable (simple) chord systems in a disk with a fixed boundary 2n-gon S, modulo S-isomorphism. Their map to simple affine arrangements with prescribed cyclic order has fibres of cardinality 2.
ideas.modern_name: Wiring diagrams / commutation classes of reduced words of w0 in S_n / higher Bruhat order B(n,2) / rhombic tilings of the 2n-gon (dual picture)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Goodman (wiring diagrams 1980); Manin–Schechtman 1989; Elnitsky 1997; Ziegler 1993; Felsner

missed.claim: Grothendieck's set C̃_st(S), stable chord systems pinned to a fixed 2n-gon S, is the same object as the set of rhombic tilings of a 2n-gon, i.e. commutation classes of reduced words of the longest permutation (Manin–Schechtman B(n,2)). He arrives at it from the topological 'découpage' of RP² along a line, around 1981. This predates the higher Bruhat order literature (1989) and Elnitsky (1997), though Goodman–Pollack's wiring diagrams already existed.
missed.quote: Soit maintenant S un ens. polygonal ... d'ordre 2n, donné une fois pour toutes. On s'intéresse aux structures de syst. stables de cordes S-épinglées (mod S-isom)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical. It documents Grothendieck working on the combinatorics of pseudoline arrangements in the same period as Goodman–Pollack. His explicit 2-sheeted cover formalism may tie into his 'polygonal' viewpoint elsewhere in cote 80. The content itself is standard.

missed.claim: The unpublished cote 80 notes show Grothendieck setting up a moduli/fibration framework for pseudoline arrangements around 1981: maps C_aff(I0) → C(I) → C(n+1), with fibres identified as orbit sets and verified by small counts. This programme is not recorded in the literature.
missed.quote: Ĩ0(ξ) ≃ ens des sommets sur ∂D = ∂X̃ (rev. à deux feuillets de Δ)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Biographical and historical interest only; no new theorem appears on this page.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a clean but standard reduction: cut along the line at infinity, get chords in a disk, fix the boundary 2n-gon, and obtain a 2:1 fibre. This is known from Goodman–Pollack and the later wiring-diagram / rhombic-tiling literature. Interest is mostly historical: Grothendieck independently working on pseudoline arrangement combinatorics around 1981.
transcription_corrections: 'Cas spécial [?] card I0 ≥ 3' is more likely '(Cas où card I0 ≥ 3)'.
'un ens. polygonal à n sommets [?] d'ordre 2n' is likely just 'un ens. polygonal à sommets, d'ordre 2n' or 'un ens. polygonal d'ordre 2n'; S has 2n vertices, not n.
On the next page 'C_off st' should read 'C_aff st'.
The marginal superscript over the struck word 'explicite' is likely 'transcrit' (hard to read); the struck phrase continuing to the next line plausibly reads 'Polygone des sommets sur ∂D'.
'systèmes de cordes stables' is better read as 'systèmes de cordes Σ̃ (stables)': 'stables' is an interlinear addition.
